=== FINDING 1 (NEW, CONFIRMED AS UNSUPPORTED, BLOCKING) -- HANDOFF.md asserts a platform impossibility that this routine's own toolset contradicts ===
HANDOFF.md item 2 reads, in full: "**THE CLOUD LOOP IS LIVE (D27).** A conductor routine picks work every 2h; a separate reviewer routine writes the gating record hourly. **No routine can create a routine, so a conductor CANNOT dispatch its reviewer -- independence is structural.**"
The load-bearing clause is "No routine can create a routine". I am a routine. The session I am running in has, in its own tool list, `create_trigger` ("Create a Routine (scheduled trigger)... create_new_session_on_fire=true -- spawns a FRESH SESSION in this environment on each firing"), `fire_trigger` ("Fire a Routine immediately, outside of its schedule"), `update_trigger` (which can replace another Routine's prompt) and `create_session`. A conductor routine running on this same account and environment would have the same list.
I DID NOT CALL ANY OF THEM. My authorization permits exactly two writes -- a review record under reviews/<pr>/ on the PR's own branch, and PR comments -- so creating, firing or editing a trigger is outside it, and I will not manufacture evidence by doing something I am not allowed to do. So I am NOT claiming "I created a routine from a routine and it worked." I am claiming the narrower and still decisive thing: the sentence states a structural impossibility, and the only evidence available to me from inside a routine points the other way. An unsupported impossibility claim is worse than an honest policy claim, because it tells every future reader there is nothing here to check.
WHY THIS IS BLOCKING RATHER THAN A NIT. It is in HANDOFF.md, the file CLAUDE.md orders every session to read FIRST, and it is the safety argument for the entire cloud review loop -- the reason a reader is told they may trust an automated AGREE. D27 itself, which this sentence cites, does NOT say this. D27 says: "The reviewer must be a SEPARATE cron entry with no trigger path from any conductor." That is a CONFIGURATION requirement someone must maintain and can verify. HANDOFF.md upgrades it into a property of the platform. D27's own paragraph warns against exactly this drift: "Not a line of prose saying 'do not review your own work' -- this repository has documented eight instances of a rule that lived only in prose being violated, including by the author who wrote it." Telling readers the mechanism is impossible is how a prose rule stops being checked.
THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE, and it does not weaken the loop: say what D27 says. E.g. "...a separate reviewer routine, a distinct cron entry with no trigger path from any conductor (D27), writes the gating record hourly. Independence rests on that configuration, not on a platform guarantee -- verify the two entries are separate." If the author has MEASURED that the platform refuses a routine-created routine, then cite the measurement (what was called, what error came back) and I withdraw this finding on sight of it.
Note in fairness: this sentence was already present at b8ab0888, the head reviewer A reviewed, and A did not charge it. It is not a regression introduced by the fix commits.

=== A NEAR-MISS I AM RECORDING RATHER THAN HIDING ===
I first drafted this finding as "the cloud loop's independence claim is false." That overstated what I measured. The tool being present in my list is not the same as a call succeeding -- the platform could reject it server-side, and the conductor's environment could differ from mine. I narrowed the finding to what I can actually stand behind (the claim is unsupported and contradicted by the available evidence, not disproved) before writing it down. Charging an innocent pull request with a stronger claim than the evidence carries is the failure mode I was warned about, and I came within one draft of it.

=== FINDING 2 (CONFIRMED, PRE-EXISTING IN MAIN, NOT CHARGED TO THIS PR) -- a superseded DISAGREE blocks lwb-lanes forever ===
Reviewer A raised this on #29, #30, #32 and #35; I reproduce it here at this head rather than inheriting it. In `lwb_lanes._review_ok` the verdict test (line 632-633) runs BEFORE the staleness test and APPENDS to `errors`. reviews/35/cloud-reviewer.json names b8ab0888, which is NOT the current reviewable head 78582c9 -- it is stale by the repo's own definition -- yet the gate still reports it as a DISAGREE failure instead of skipping it. So: a stale AGREE is correctly ignored, a stale DISAGREE is not. The author fixed both of A's findings and the gate cannot notice. Nothing the author can do on this branch clears it; only A superseding its own record at the new head, or a fix to lwb_lanes.py, will.

=== FINDING 3 (CONFIRMED BY REVIEWER A, RE-CONFIRMED BY CONSTRUCTION HERE) -- my own id collides with the author's on "buildcraft" ===
My routine mandates the reviewer_id string "reviewer-cloud-routine-b-buildcraft". proof/35.json's `author` is "conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19". Both legitimately embed the repository's own name, so the set-based collision rule in lwb_lanes sees the shared segment "buildcraft" (10 characters, at or above MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8) and rejects the record as a likely self-review. It is a FALSE POSITIVE: reviewer A's routine and mine and the conductor are three different sessions. I MEASURED IT MYSELF rather than inheriting reviewer A's probe, by calling the gate's own collision function on my own id pair:
    $ python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import lwb_lanes as L; print(L._shared_long_segment('reviewer-cloud-routine-b-buildcraft-01AteicM6ZQ6P34BWuoN9jwB-2026-09-19','conductor-track-a-buildcraft-01PDRLaG51Uor9D8wTtnpJ25-2026-09-19'))"
    buildcraft
A detail worth recording, because it hid the collision from the CI output: running the full gate at this head reports ONLY "verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'" for my record and never mentions the shared segment, so _review_ok stops at the first error rather than reporting both. Anyone reading only the job log would learn my verdict blocks and would NOT learn that my AGREE would have blocked too.
I DID NOT RENAME MYSELF AROUND IT. Dropping "buildcraft" from my id would turn this gate green and would be falsifying an identifier to pass a validator -- the one thing my instructions and reviews/README.md both forbid. The fix belongs in the gate (exclude non-identifying segments such as the repo or org name from the comparison) or in the id convention (stop embedding the repository name), decided deliberately and recorded. reviews/README.md already names this exact failure mode as the reason the floor sits at 8 -- "the failure mode that gets a gate disabled". It is no longer hypothetical; it has now hit two distinct reviewer routines on four pull requests.
COMBINED HONEST SUMMARY OF FINDINGS 2 AND 3: lwb-lanes on this branch cannot be cleared by either cloud reviewer routine, in either direction, for reasons that are properties of the gate and not of this PR's work. That is worth an owner decision, and it means nobody should wait on a reviewer routine to unblock #35.
